observation.visible_scene: A single large, irregularly shaped iridescent soap bubble dominates the right and center of the frame, floating in front of a backdrop of leafy trees (green foliage on the left, reddish-brown leaves and bare branches on the right, pale sky behind). A thin diagonal wand rod and a curved film boundary are visible at the right edge of the bubble. A fixed watermark text sits in the top-left corner. The bubble's surface shows swirling bands of magenta, green, cyan and yellow.
visible_changes: The bubble's outline morphs slowly and continuously: the rounded lobe on the left edge drifts slightly leftward and its contour smooths, while the lower edge rises and a distinct rounded lobe develops at the lower-right.
Iridescent color bands swirl and reposition across the film (the central green band shifts and magenta spreads) without the bubble popping.
The right-side film boundary and the area around the visible wand rod undulate, with a secondary bulge/tail changing shape.
The trees, branches and watermark remain in identical positions across all frames, indicating a stationary camera and a static background.
No editing cut or abrupt change is present; the motion is a continuous gentle deformation and color flow of the bubble film.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the bubble was just released from a wand or will subsequently pop; any operator or hand holding the rod is outside the frame.
The cause of the film's undulations (air movement vs. wand motion) is not visible.
The state of the bubble before t=0 and after t=3.33s is unknown.
uncertain_details: Whether the left-edge shift represents a small overall translation of the bubble or purely local deformation is hard to separate.
Subtle color-pattern changes may reflect film-thickness variation rather than lateral motion of the film.
